title: Your coding agent gets a boundary.
summary: GitHub has made local sandboxing generally available across Copilot CLI, its app, and VS Code Agent Host sessions.
why: Developers can restrict an agent’s file, network and credential access instead of giving every command the same reach as their own shell.
takeaways: Policies cover filesystem, network and credential access.
Microsoft eXecution Container translates policies into native operating-system controls.
Tool isolation is separate from model execution.

title: Local models, one less setup detour.
summary: Copilot CLI can discover supported models from a running Ollama instance through its model picker.
why: It makes an existing local model easier to select, but does not install Ollama, download models or automatically enable offline mode.
takeaways: Available starting in CLI version 1.0.94-0.
Models must support tool calling and streaming.
Review the provider and endpoint before adding a model.

title: Big changes. Smaller pull requests.
summary: Stacked pull requests are generally available on GitHub, with improvements to rebasing, review and merging.
why: Teams can break a large change into reviewable pieces while keeping their dependencies visible.
takeaways: Approvals can survive rebases when the reviewed code is unchanged.
Stack context stays visible in the pull request header.
Available on all github.com plans; Enterprise Server support is forthcoming.

title: Secret scanning widens its net.
summary: GitHub adds secret detectors for providers including Lovable and Supabase.
why: New detector coverage can help surface accidentally committed credentials. Review the official list for supported token types and availability.
takeaways: The announcement lists newly supported providers.
Detection is a safety net, not a replacement for keeping secrets out of source control.

title: A first npm release can wait for review.
summary: Staged publishing now supports creating new npm packages directly from automated workflows.
why: A maintainer can review and promote the first version before anyone can install it.
takeaways: Supports public scoped, public unscoped and private scoped packages.
The first version enters a staged queue.
Package settings and trusted publishing can be configured after creation.

title: Make accessibility easier to find.
summary: GitHub highlights accessibility statements on repository overviews.
why: A visible statement gives users a starting point for understanding accessibility coverage and known limitations.
takeaways: The repository overview can surface the project’s accessibility statement.
An accessibility statement should describe actual testing and known gaps.

title: Firefox moves to a two-week rhythm.
summary: Mozilla announced a shorter release cycle, beginning with Firefox 155 on 1 September 2026.
why: More predictable updates aim to deliver completed fixes sooner; Mozilla says this does not mean twice as many features.
takeaways: The cadence changes from four weeks to two.
The stated aim is more predictable delivery of fixes and completed features.

title: Astro 6 puts content infrastructure first.
summary: Astro 6 brings a built-in Fonts API, Content Security Policy support and live content collections.
why: Content-heavy sites gain tools for self-hosted fonts and externally managed content, alongside a redesigned development server.
takeaways: The development server uses Vite’s Environment API.
Live collections support request-time content fetching.
Node 22 or later is required.
